source.title: A Compositional Theory of Curvature in Probabilistic Circuits
source.authors: Hrithik Suresh; Sahil Sidheekh; Shelar Parth Vijay; Z. Yasir; S. Natarajan; N. C. Krishnan

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses sharpness-aware learning to build and evaluate a regularizer for probabilistic circuits. Its results concern curvature regularization in PCs, but do not test the specific claim versions, which concern neural-network memorization, architecture, optimizers, batches, dropout, magnitude-aware perturbations, or memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on probabilistic-circuit likelihood and curvature regularization. Those results do not measure any listed claim version. Cited findings from other work are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study uses sharpness-based regularization to develop a probabilistic-circuit learner. Its Hessian-trace and likelihood results do not test V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap ranking, or convolutional networks, and do not address the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly captures the main conclusion: global curvature contributions factor into contextual usage and intrinsic local curvature, and local-curvature gating mitigates underfitting while preserving tractable EM learning. Its statement about retaining robustness is an abstract-level assertion; the supplied experiments do not directly evaluate robustness.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and regularizes curvature in probabilistic circuits trained with EM; it does not use the neural-network methods or measures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Data availability changes the reported effect: global trace regularization can improve likelihood with limited data but frequently degrades it as data increase. Node-selection criteria also change fit: selecting by local curvature preserves fit more effectively than selecting by global contribution.

fits_no_version.finding: At full data, global trace regularization lowers test likelihood on 18 of 20 probabilistic-circuit benchmarks. Local-curvature gating generally recovers fit, although it does not outperform global regularization on every dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In probabilistic circuits, allocating trace regularization using local curvature can mitigate underfitting caused by uniform global regularization.

record.problems: The reported experiments use probabilistic circuits rather than the neural-network systems named by the claim. Several findings are described qualitatively or in figures without precise numerical comparisons in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were omitted. Figure-only sweeps and detailed per-dataset table values were not transcribed because they do not bear on a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy in the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization and local-connectivity qualifications.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effects on classifier test error across data-size and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Flatter circuits with worse test likelihood do not challenge V7: this study changes the model class, curvature measure, training fit, and outcome, and does not evaluate the specified correlational ranking.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexist in the specified neural networks.
Test error after widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons and stated tuning qualifications.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on classifier test error, including training-set and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation tolerance and its ranking of train-test gaps in the specified convolutional family.
Removing and retraining after removing memorized examples.

rows.subject: HCLT
rows.operation_detail: Global trace regularization versus unregularized training, evaluated on full-data DEBD benchmarks.
rows.measure: Test log-likelihood; paper reports global trace regularization degrades performance on 18 datasets and improves on 2.
rows.value: Global trace regularization improves on only 2 datasets and degrades performance on the remaining 18.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over 5 random seeds; no uncertainty for the 18/2 count stated.
rows.locator: Experiments, Q3: Underfitting and recovery; Table 2
rows.note: This is a probabilistic-circuit likelihood result, not one of the listed neural-network claim versions.
rows.check: The 2 improvements and 18 degradations agree with Table 2, but measure probabilistic-circuit test likelihood rather than any listed version.

rows.subject: HCLT
rows.operation_detail: Local-curvature-gated trace regularization compared with global trace regularization and unregularized training.
rows.measure: Test log-likelihood; gated method outperforms global trace regularization and matches or improves upon the unregularized model on a majority of datasets.
rows.baseline: Global trace regularization and unregularized model
rows.value: Gated method outperforms global trace regularization and matches or improves upon the unregularized model on the majority of datasets.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over 5 random seeds; no uncertainty for the majority statement stated.
rows.locator: Experiments, Q3: Underfitting and recovery; Table 2
rows.note: The result concerns the proposed regularizer in probabilistic circuits; it does not test any listed version.
rows.check: This is the study's proposed method compared with baselines, not a claim-testing row. Its blanket superiority over global regularization also needs correcting: on bbc, gated likelihood is -260.07 versus -256.40 for global regularization, so gated performs worse.

rows.subject: PC with Gaussian input distributions and 16 sum and input units
rows.operation_detail: Unregularized maximum likelihood, global trace regularization, and adaptive local-curvature gating from the same initialization.

conditions.value: 50 training samples; 800 test samples drawn only from the Gaussian mixture

rows.measure: Train NLL, test NLL, and exact Hessian trace; unregularized training attains the lowest train NLL but higher test NLL and curvature, while global regularization sacrifices train and test fit; adaptive gating reaches better test fit than global regularization at lower curvature.
rows.baseline: Unregularized model and global trace regularization
rows.value: Adaptive gating reaches a region with better test fit than uniform global regularization and lower curvature.
rows.locator: Supplementary Material, A 2D Synthetic Data Distribution; Figure 10
rows.note: The text gives qualitative trajectory comparisons without numerical values. This is a probabilistic-circuit result, not a listed version.
rows.check: This is a proposed-method comparison outside the listed versions. Correct the training condition to 50 Gaussian-mixture samples plus eight ring-noise samples, totaling 58; the 800 test samples exclude the noise.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
